'''Anthony F. Hill''' is a Professor of [[Chemistry]] at the [[Research School of Chemistry]] of the [[Australian National University]].<ref name="Profile at Australian Nat Univ">{{Cite web
  | last = Research School of Chemistry
  | title = Profile of Professor Hill
  | year = 2010
  | url = http://chemistry.anu.edu.au/rsc/people/anthony-hill/
  | access-date = 2010-05-27 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100529023120/http://chemistry.anu.edu.au/rsc/people/anthony-hill/| archive-date= 29 May 2010 | url-status= dead}}</ref> He specializes in [[synthetic chemistry|synthetic]], [[organometallic]] and [[coordination chemistry]].<ref name="Hill pubs.">{{Cite web
  | last = Research School of Chemistry
  | title = Publications of Anthony F. Hill 1996-2014 (with doi links)
  | year = 2014
  | url = http://chemistry.anu.edu.au/people/anthony-hill
  | access-date = 29 August 2017 }}</ref>
He is the author of a textbook on the subject of the organometallic chemistry of the [[transition metals]]<ref name="Organotransition Metal Chemistry">{{cite book |title=Organotransition Metal Chemistry |last=Hill |first=Anthony F. |year=2002 |publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry |location=Cambridge, UK |isbn=978-0-85404-622-5 |id = RSC Tutorial Text #7, Organotransition Metal Chemistry}}</ref> and since 1995 has been an editor of the [[scientific journal]]/book series ''[[Advances in Organometallic Chemistry]]''.<ref name="Adv Orgmet Chem">{{Cite web
| title = ADVANCES IN ORGANOMETALLIC CHEMISTRY, 59 | url = http://www.elsevier.com/wps/find/bookdescription.cws_home/720863/description#description |date= 2010-04-29 | access-date = 2010-05-27 }}</ref> He is a [[Fellow#Learned or professional societies, or speciality training|fellow]] of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]].<ref name="Hill pubs."/>

==Education==
Hill graduated from the [[University of Auckland]] with a [[Master of Science]] (Honours) and was awarded the title of [[Dr. rer. nat.]] from the [[University of Bayreuth]] for his doctoral thesis.<ref name="Profile at Australian Nat Univ"/>

==Academic career==
Prior to being appointed to the position of Professor at the Research School of Chemistry in 2001, Hill held positions at [[Imperial College]] (1992–2000), the [[University of Warwick]] (1988–1991) and the [[University of Bristol]] (1986–1988).<ref name="Profile at Australian Nat Univ"/> At the Research School of Chemistry, Hill is the leader of the 'Synthetic Organometallic and Coordination Chemistry' group<ref>{{Cite web
 |title=Synthetic Organometallic and Coordination Chemistry 
 |url=http://chemistry.anu.edu.au/rsc/inorganic-chemistry/synthetic-organometallic-and-coordination-chemistr/ 
 |access-date=2010-05-27 
 |url-status=dead 
 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100721214936/http://chemistry.anu.edu.au/rsc/inorganic-chemistry/synthetic-organometallic-and-coordination-chemistr/ 
 |archive-date=2010-07-21 
}}</ref> and teaches an [[undergraduate]] organometallic chemistry course.<ref>
{{Cite web| title= Chemical Structure and Reactivity II| url= http://chemistry.anu.edu.au/doc/2nd-year/chemical-structure-and-reactivity-ii/| access-date= 2010-05-27| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100501145039/http://chemistry.anu.edu.au/doc/2nd-year/chemical-structure-and-reactivity-ii/| archive-date= 1 May 2010| url-status= dead}}
</ref>

== Research interests ==
Tony Hill's research interests investigate the nature of [[metal carbon bonding]] and endeavor to develop an understanding of the interaction of carbon with transition and main group metals.<ref name="Profile at Australian Nat Univ"/> The organometallic chemistry of complexes of transition metals with poly(methimazolyl)borato and other related ligands has in recent time been the subject of much of Tony Hill's work. One of Tony Hill's special topics is the chemistry (and synthesis of) the metallaboratranes. Using [[iridium]],<ref>{{cite journal | title=Formation of Metallaboratranes: The Missing Link. The First Iridaboratranes, [IrH(CO)(PPh3){κ3-B,S,S'-B(mt)2R}](Ir→B) (mt = Methimazolyl, R = mt, H) | author=Ian R. Crossley, Anthony F. Hill and Anthony C. Willis | journal=[[Organometallics]] | date=12 February 2005 | volume=24 | issue=6 | pages=1062–1064 | doi=10.1021/om040128f}}</ref> [[platinum]], [[osmium]],<ref>M.R.S.J Foreman, A.F. Hill, A.J.P. White and D.J. Williams, ''Organometallics'', 2004, volume 23, issue 4, pages 913-916</ref> [[rhodium]],<ref>I.R. Crossley, A.F. Hill and A.C. Willis, "Metallaboratranes: tris(methimazolyl)borane complexes of rhodium(I)",
 ''Organometallics'', 2006, volume 25, issue 1, pages 289-299, {{doi|10.1021/om050772+}}</ref> and [[ruthenium]] and other [[transition metals]] Tony Hill has been able to form compounds containing [[Organoboron chemistry|metal boron bonds]].{{citation needed|date=November 2019}}

== Publications ==
As of May 2010, Hill has authored more than 220 scientific journal articles most of which relate to the field of [[organometallic chemistry]].<ref name="Hill pubs."/>

In 1986, with Prof. Dr. Max Herberhold at the [[University of Bayreuth]], Hill published the first account of complex containing an unsubstituted [[sulfine]].<ref>{{Cite journal
  | last = Herberhold
  | first = Max
  | author2 = Hill, Anthony F.
  | title = Der erste metallkomplexes des unsubstituierten sulfins, CH2SO
  | journal = Journal of Organometallic Chemistry
  | volume = 309
  | issue = 1–2
  | pages = C29–C33
  | date = 1986-04-25
  | issn = 0022-328X
  | doi = 10.1016/S0022-328X(00)99597-4
 }}</ref>

Hill has recently published several papers concerning the nature of [[carbo-borane]] and ruthenium-borane interactions. Most recently, Caldwell and Cordiner collaborated with Hill on a paper entitled "Phosphino and phosphonito carbyne complexes"<ref>"Phosphino and phosphonito carbyne complexes: [Mo(≡CX)(CO)2{HB(pzMe2)3}] (X = PPh2, P(=O)(OEt)2; pz = pyrazol-1-yl)" Caldwell L.M., Cordiner R.L., Hill A.F., Wagler J. "A bridging selenoacyl complex via alkynylselenolatoalkylidyne rearrangement". ''Organometallics'' (2010), 29(7), 1526 - 1529. {{doi|10.1021/om901079n}}</ref>

Hill is author of a textbook entitled ''Organotransition Metal Chemistry''.<ref name="Organotransition Metal Chemistry"/>
